key_insight: A hydrogen-informed Rice-Beltz model predicts crack-tip dislocation emission under mixed-mode loading by coupling hydrogen-induced stress-field interactions with a transition-state barrier for nucleation.
engineering_relevance: It provides a parameter-free way to estimate when hydrogen will shift the crack-tip response from cleavage toward plasticity, helping assess hydrogen embrittlement risk in crystalline solids.
method: Extends the Rice-Beltz framework to mixed-mode I+II crack-tip loading.
Includes elastic interaction between interstitial hydrogen dilatation fields and the incipient dislocation core.
Uses local strain energy density minimization plus transition-state theory to derive critical stress intensity factors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports closed-form predictions that reproduce a non-monotonic relationship between the most probable stress intensity factor and hydrogen concentration, along with dependence on loading rate, slip angle, and hydrogen content.
watch_item: The model is atomistically informed but still analytical, so its accuracy depends on how well the assumed core energetics and hydrogen-field interactions represent the specific material and loading path.
paper_title: A hydrogen-informed Rice-Beltz model for crack-tip dislocation emission under mixed-mode loading
